purpose: How much of a cutting-error model lies below a chosen tolerance?
meaning: Subtract the mean error from the threshold, divide by the positive standard deviation, and evaluate the standard normal CDF. The density curve supplies a height per millimetre; its accumulated area supplies probability.

definition.setting: A workshop measures signed cutting errors in millimetres around a target length. Its chosen model has mean error μ and standard deviation σ. Slide a tolerance x across the density, then follow the standardized distance z into the area below x.

signature.μ: Mean of the declared normal error model in mm
signature.σ: Positive standard deviation of the declared model in mm
signature.f(x): Probability density height per mm at the threshold
signature.F(x): Cumulative probability of an error at or below the threshold

conditions: A declared normal model describes signed cutting errors in mm, with μ from −2 to 2 and σ from 0.25 to 2. Probability is area, not density height or probability at one point. The fixed density window −10 to 10 mm omits tails without renormalizing. The full CDF is approximated by 32/64-node Gauss–Legendre quadrature and tested against erfc; measured-grid accuracy is not a proof of a global error bound. No normality or central-limit theorem is inferred.
